conviction_note: The evidence balances: a consistent 4-6% beat-versus-guide pattern and a likely Q4 guide that can start to include Design Agent/Weave (GA 2026-10-06) on one side, and the 10-Q showing Q2 billings flat q/q with deferred revenue down q/q plus the August doubling of AI credit allowances (an effective price cut) on the other. The 4-6% beat pattern is widely known (Stifel expects 3-4 pts), the name sold a 6% beat-and-raise by 14.85% in August, and 25-delta skew is +11.8 vol points to the downside. So p_up sits at 50 while abs_move stays at the 12.6-13.2% implied/median scale. The fundamental read (print about +2.5% over a $376.5M consensus) and the reaction read (0) disagree on purpose. Findings sum to -0.2.

findings.finding: Figma has beaten its own revenue-guide midpoint by 3.9% (Q3'25: $274.2M vs $263-265M guide), 5.5% (Q1'26: $333.4M vs $315-317M) and 6.0% (Q2'26: $370.1M vs $348-350M). The same beat on the $374M Q3 midpoint gives $389-396M, against a published consensus of $376.5M that sits only 0.7% above the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26: a 6.0% beat over guide plus a $40M FY raise, and the stock fell 14.85%. Q1'26: a 5.5% beat plus a raise, and it rose 13.24%. Q4'25: beat, +6.9% close-to-close (it was down about 11% intraday per startupfortune). Q3'25: 3.9% beat, +4.48%. The beat itself has not set the sign; guide and margin did.
findings.why_not_priced: Published consensus ($376.5M) is set close to the guide, as is usual. If the street fully priced the beat pattern, consensus would sit near $390M. But Stifel publicly expects 3-4 pts (2026-11-04 Investing.com preview), so the buy-side bar is probably around $385-389M and most of this is in the whisper. What is left is the gap between a 3-4 pt and a 5-6 pt beat.
findings.independence: Q1 guide and actual: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1579878/000162828026009024/fy25pressrelease.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579878/000162828026035087/q126pressrelease.htm. Stifel's 3-4 pt expectation: https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/figma-earnings-on-deck-can-ai-products-offset-competition-93CH-5680410. These are all company documents plus one broker view; finding 2 argues the other way from a different company document.

findings.finding: The Q2'26 10-Q deferred-revenue rollforward shows billings of $369.2M against revenue of $370.1M, with deferred revenue down q/q ($627.7M to $626.8M). In Q2'25 billings ($276.2M) ran $26.6M above revenue, and in Q3'25 ($314.6M) $40.4M above. Q2 billings were up only 0.9% q/q (Q1'26 $365.8M) and +34% y/y, against +48% revenue growth. So Q2 revenue ran ahead of bookings, and the guide's +1% q/q may be closer to real than the beat history suggests. Offsetting: RPO was $687.0M, up 53% y/y from $448.8M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Figma reports no billings metric, so there is no direct reaction record. The one adjacent case is Q2: the guide implying only +1% q/q sequential growth was the line analysts (Goldman, Citi) pressed on, and the stock fell 14.85%. Management attributed it to lapping the March 2025 pricing changes.
findings.why_not_priced: Billings is not in the press release or on the aggregator pages. Previews quote the revenue beats and the guide, not the deferred walk. If this were priced, previews would discuss calculated billings or a deferred-revenue decline. None of the four previews read did. Partly priced through the general worry about deceleration and the 15% drop on the guide.
findings.independence: Q3'25 rollforward from a different filing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1579878/000162828025049683/fig-20250930.htm (billings $314.6M on revenue $274.2M). Analysts pressing on the small sequential guide: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/figma-q2-earnings-call-puts-ai-monetization-broadening-focus. Shares a document with nothing else filed here.

findings.finding: From 2026-08-25 Figma raised the credits included in its AI add-on to 2x (Pro) and 1.6x (Organization/Enterprise) at no price change and updated pay-as-you-go pricing. It is an effective price cut on AI credit revenue inside Q3, the first quarter after Q2 became the first full quarter of AI-credit monetization.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AI-credit news has moved the stock both ways: enforcement on 2026-03-18 drew 'demand-friction' selling per rallies.ai (2026-03-27), and the Q1 print that showed credit monetization rose 13.24%. No print has yet reported AI-credit revenue as a number.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Piper called it an effective price cut on 2026-10-26 and still raised its FY26 AI-credit revenue estimates. What is unpriced is the size of the Q3 hit, because Figma does not disclose AI-credit revenue. It also landed after the Q3 guide of 2026-08-05 was set, unless management already planned it.
findings.independence: Piper Sandler note 2026-10-26: https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/piper-sandler-reiterates-figma-stock-rating-on-ai-credit-growth-93CH-4973249 (it calls this an effective price cut but raises estimates, so it argues toward a small size).

findings.finding: Design Agent and Weave went from open beta (no credits charged) to general availability on 2026-10-06 and now draw Figma AI credits. Figma's guidance excludes 'products still in beta or early-access programs', so the Q4/FY guide given tonight is the first that can include them.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has set the sign: Q1'26 FY raise of about $54M at the midpoint gave +13.24%; Q2'26 FY raise of $40M with op income held gave -14.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: Stifel publicly calls AI upside 'more of a 4Q/2027 event than 3Q', so the street expects it later and some of it is in expectations. What is not known is whether management puts these GA products into the Q4 guide or keeps excluding them, and the guide-exclusion language makes that a live question tonight. If it were priced, the skew would not be paying 11.8 vol points for downside on a name whose guide is about to widen.
findings.independence: Guide-exclusion language in the Q2 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579878/000162828026053331/q226pressrelease.htm. GA and credits: https://fourweekmba.com/ai-figma-design-agent-leaves-beta-now-draws-ai-credits/. Stifel timing view: https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/figma-earnings-on-deck-can-ai-products-offset-competition-93CH-5680410.

findings.finding: FY26 non-GAAP operating income guidance was held at $125-135M while revenue guidance rose $40M. H1 delivered $88.2M (Q1 $52.1M at 16%, Q2 $36.1M at 10%), so the guide implies only $37-47M for H2, roughly a 5% margin on about $760-780M of H2 revenue. That sets a low Q3 bar for operating income, the line the stock sold off on in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26: EPS $0.08 vs $0.04 consensus, yet the stock fell 14.85% 'as operating costs rose and margins compressed' (startupfortune 2026-11-04). In February it beat and fell about 11% intraday. Holding the op guide while raising revenue was read as investment-heavy and sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Arithmetic on three company releases that previews do not do. Consensus Q3 EPS of $0.05, down from $0.08, already embeds lower margins, so a Q3 op-income beat is likely. The sign rests on whether FY op income is raised (positive) or held again (a repeat of August), so it is a small net positive with a wide band. Lands inside what the company guided.
findings.independence: Q2 op income $36.1M and FY guide: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579878/000162828026053331/q226pressrelease.htm (same company series; one finding).

findings.finding: Insider supply continued into the print: 25 Form 4s and 14 Form 144s from 2026-08-12 to 2026-11-03, including four Form 4s and a Form 144 on 2026-11-03. CEO Dylan Field has sold under a March 2026 10b5-1 plan covering up to 1M shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Form 4 headlines were cited as weighing on down days (rallies.ai 2026-03-27). No print-day reaction is attributable.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is routine, plan-based, and has run every month since the lock-ups ended. It matters only as overhang that can cap a positive reaction.

findings.finding: Estimates and sentiment drifted lower into the print: EPS estimates were down 0.91% over two months, Stifel cut its target to $22 from $25 and Wells Fargo to $30 from $34, and 10 of 16 analysts rate Hold. Competitive pressure from Anthropic's Claude Design (April), Google Stitch (March) and Canva AI 2.0 (April) is the cited reason.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Competitive launches moved the stock between prints (Stitch, 2026-03-19). On prints, results outweighed competition headlines: Q1 rose 13% after the April launches.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced: this is the wire. Filed because a low sentiment bar is the context a beat is judged against. It could also argue the bar is easy to clear, so it is sized near zero.

baseline_tension: The findings net to about zero and do not fight the +11.8 put skew or the -4.6% five-day slide. The positive items (beat pattern, GA products entering the guide, a low H2 margin bar) are what a buyer of the skew is betting against, and the August reaction shows those items have been sold before. So p_up stays at 50 and the magnitude stays at the implied scale.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): beat-pattern finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6, because a 6% beat-and-raise was sold 14.85% in August.

Lesson 7 (positioning/skew): the two positive guidance findings sit against +11.8 vol points of put skew; Design Agent/Weave cut from +1.0 to +0.7 and the margin-bar finding from +0.5 to +0.3. p_up moved from 52 to 50.
Lesson 5 (proxy): Adobe read-through cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
'What has worked' (deferred-revenue walk read off the filing): the billings finding was left at -1.0, the largest negative, because it rests on a primary document no aggregator carries.
Lesson 7 short-interest check: SI 7% of shares out, 3.85 DTC, not crowded, so no negative was shrunk for squeeze risk.
